answers.why: Capture skill's entry rules (find meow, read the repo's rules file, who, leave Cat Herder); it works as shipped and no reader rule or skill files work into a queue.
The mid-task capture procedure (one exchange, level by signal, split, duplicate check); it fits reader rule 4 ("bookkeeping, not new scope") and the reader has no capture skill.
Queue-and-claim before doing asked work, per focus; a workflow of the capture skill with no reader equivalent.
Rescue session procedure (read queue, match, add, report counts); one-shot workflow of the capture skill that the reader lacks.
Riffing mode keeps replies to a line and builds nothing on unread replies; part of the capture skill and not in any reader rule.

The herd skill (pairs, hikes, status footer, launcher rules); its "Which model a session you start runs on" starts a session, not a subagent dispatch, so it does not break examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rule 6.
Associate role file of the herd skill (declare a domain, answer on the item); works with meow and the reader has nothing like it.
Two sentences saying when a handoff happens; they only introduce the steps judged in u9 to u12.
The retiring-session handoff steps; they ask to "push anything you haven't" and run `meow herd clean` only on the owner's go-ahead, so they sit inside examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 1.
The staying member checks the new session's readback before confirming; part of the handoff role and new to the reader.
New-session rules (take no items until confirmed, own branch name, never write in the starting directory); part of the handoff role.
Fixed chat lines for each handoff step; the handoff role's reporting format, which the reader has no equivalent of.
Reviewer role header (independent judge from the queue and commits, rigor, the repo's rules win); template filled by pair start, works as shipped.
Reviewer setup step (make a checkout, check the pair, stop); a template part of the reviewer role.
The per-review procedure (read note, review the named commits, attack, one verdict); a review workflow the reader's release-notes skill and rules do not cover.
Reviewer limits (binding verdict, no edits to the worker's code, "Never use `--force`"); tool-specific and stricter than, not against, the reader's rules.
How a reviewer is started and stopped (the worker stops the pair, the owner has the last word); pair lifecycle of the herd skill.
Rigor-build reviewer checks ("Does the test pin the claim?", cite file:line); part of the reviewer role and echoes examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rule 3 without being only that.

The worker's pair procedure (claim, branch names, done note, wait, reopen, hike, stop); core of the herd skill. Its "never run `meow herd clean` on your own" matches examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 1.

Rigor-build worker rules (raw output in the done note, "Blocked is a real answer"); also carries five coding rules that overlap examples/reader/rules/engineering.md rules 1, 2 and 5, and it defers to the project's own debt marker, so no conflict.
Intro to the voice skill plus a repeat of the find-the-command paragraph; wraps the persona switch.
/herder only switches the cat voice on or off; a persona setting.
Cat names and cat-voice wording in chat; persona.
Cat-voice confirmation lines ("Mrrp. Boxed."); persona.
One line of voice wording for a cat that leaves; persona.
Cat-voice handoff lines; persona twin of u12.
Rules for the voice's euphemisms; persona.

The queue skill's setup and conventions (placements, never the code branch, Field Trip, voice-reading rules); it asks before irreversible steps, as examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 5 wants, and the reader has no queue.
Everyday queue operations and the ready check ("don't build the old version", "Never use `--force` on your own"); works with meow and fits the reader's scope rule 4.
The Overheard block and `For you:` line format for relayed messages; a reporting convention of the queue skill the reader lacks.
A sample ledger entry showing the format; example output only.
The question ledger and the rule that a skipped question is "unread, not answered"; it agrees with examples/reader/rules/safety.md rule 5 and adds a procedure.
The /meow command runs one quoted meow call and prints the output; it works as shipped and the single-quoting stops argument injection.
